title: SA/66/2019 of ASHOK KUMAR MALHTORA Vs RAJKUMAR

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 66 of 2019
Sri Ashok Kumar Malhotra and others ..... Defendant/Appellants
Versus
Sri Rajkumar and others .... Plaintiff/Respondents
Present :
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate assisted by Ms. Rajni Supyal, Advocate for the
appellants.

Judgment Reserved : 22nd May, 2019
Judgment Delivered: 17th July, 2019
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 This is defendants' Second Appeal, wherein, they have
questioned the validity of the judgment and decree dated 7th May,
2019, as rendered by the 1st Additional District Judge, Dehradun, in
Civil Appeal No. 105 of 2001, Rajkumars and others Vs. Haveli Ram
Malhotra and others, whereby, the First Appeal preferred by the
plaintiffs/ respondents has been allowed and, as a consequence
thereto, the judgment and decree dated 26th July, 2001, as rendered by
the Civil Judge, Senior Division / FTC, 7th, Dehradun, dismissing the
Suit No.60 of 1998, Rajkumars and others Vs. Haveli Ram Malhotra
and others as well as the judgment with regard to the decreeing of the
counter claim preferred by the defendants/appellants under Order 8
Rule 6-A of the C.P.C. has been dismissed by the First Appellate
Court and as a consequence thereto, the suit of plaintiffs/respondents
has been decreed.
2. Precisely, the case as pleaded before the Court below was
in relation to the property, more particularly, described as property,
lying in Khasra No.49, having an area of 0.94 hectares situated in
Village Harawala Dehradun, over which, admittedly, as per the plaint
case itself, one late Mr. Sahbuddin was the recorded bhumidhar,
recorded in Shreni-1 Ka of the Zamindari Abolition Act, 1950.

2
3. It is an admitted case that the plaintiff as he then was, i.e.
late Shabuddin, he had executed a registered sale deed on 29th
January, 1966, by virtue of which, late Mr. Shabuddin, had conveyed
a part of the land constituting of 1 bigha, i.e. equivalent to 0.77
hectares of land in favour of the predecessors of the defendants/
appellants, Mr. Haveli Ram. It is the case of the defendants/
appellants that after the aforesaid purchase made by them on 29th
January, 1966, late Mr. Haveli Ram had constructed his house, Aata
Chaki and a Dhann Machine, which have been more particularly
described by figure 'ABCDE' in the plaint map. The principal
plaintiff/respondent met with sad demise on 4th November, 1996 and,
as a consequence of his death, remaining piece of land, i.e. Khasra
No. 49, having an area of 0.24 hectares, remained vested with the
heirs of late Shahbuddin, who are the defendant/ appellants, herein,
which has been shown in the plaint map by figure 'ABFG'.
4. On account of the fact that the defendants/appellants, the
purchasers, made endeavor to encroach upon the remaining part of left
over land of Khasra No.49, having an area of 0.24 hectares, the
plaintiffs/ respondents had to issue notices to the defendants/
appellants through their counsel to desist from their activity of illegal
interference over the land lying in the Northern side of their plot
which has been sold to them by late Mr. Shahbuddin and not to
demolish the three feet high wall existing, as shown by figure 'A' and
'B', as shown in the plaint map.
5. The plaintiffs/respondents contended that when the
defendants/appellants had tried to make a forceful interference over
the remaining part of the land, i.e. 0.24 hectares of Khasra No. 49, the
plaintiffs/respondents, the sellers had approached the Revenue
Authorities praying from them to demarcate the land under Section 41
of the Land Revenue Act, 1901, so that the alleged claim of ownership
over the remaining part of the land of the plaintiffs/ respondents by
defendants/appellants, may be resolved. Consequent to the

3
application submitted by the plaintiffs/ respondents, the Assistant
Record Officer is shown to have conducted a spot inspection and
measurement of the land, in question, and got it demarcated and the
land which was sold to the predecessors of the defendants/appellants
to the extent of 0.077 hectares. While performing the measurement,
the Assistant Record Officer along with the help of other Revenue
Authorities, i.e. including the Revenue Inspector had laid khuta
(pillars) over the land lying in the share of the plaintiffs/respondents,
the sellers and particularly by demarcating the disputed portion, i.e.
the wall which was extending from point 'A' to 'B' which was sought
to be encroached by the defendants/appellants by demolishing the
wall. It was the case of the plaintiffs/respondents before the Court
below that at the time when the first inspection was conducted by the
Revenue Officials, in fact, the defendants/appellants who were present
on the spot, in question, had never raised any objection of any nature
whatsoever on the act of fixing khutas by Revenue Officials, and they
had rather admitted the existence of the wall as well as the iron angle
placed on it, which demarcated the property, in question, of the
parties.
6. Owing to the no objection being raised by the
defendants/appellants, the plaintiffs/respondents, the sellers were of
the view that in fact, the propriety of the ownership of Khasra No. 49,
so far it relates to the rights of the plaintiffs/respondents, over the land
demarcated is concerned and that stands admitted that the controversy
did not stand survived at that stage.
7. However, when still the act of interference over the
property, in question, despite demarcation by Revenue Officials,
continued at the behest of the defendants/ appellants, herein, it is the
case of the plaintiffs/respondents that with the consent of the
defendants/appellants, they got conducted the inspection/demarcation
by the revenue authority for the second time and in the inspection

4
which was held in their presence, yet again, the same position
emerged as it was found in the report of the Assistant Revenue
Officer, which was submitted earlier, who have demarcated the land,
when the first inspection was conducted by them.
8. The plaintiffs/respondents when found that despite of the
second inspection which was unanimously held in the presence of
both the parties with their consent, when still the act of interference by
the defendants/appellants, the purchasers continued, the necessity
arose for the plaintiffs/ respondents to institute a suit for a grant of
decree of permanent injunction on 11th March, 1998, which was
registered as Suit No. 60 of 1998, Rajkumr and others Vs. Haveli Ram
Malhotra and others.
9. In order to give a cause of action for institution of the
suit, it was pleaded in para 10 of the plaint that the defendants/
appellants have started their endeavours of interference by removing
the brick of three feet high wall and when the same was objected by
the plaintiffs/ respondents, they threatened to encroach upon the land
which was left over by the predecessors of the plaintiffs/respondents
after the sale deed was executed in favour of predecessors of the
defendants/appellants. Lastly, when the efforts and act of removing
the bricks were not stopped by the defendants/ appellants, the cause of
action arose for them for instituting the suit when despite of the
complaint being raised to the Police Official on 10th March, 1998, the
act of encroachment by defendants/appellants persisted. Hence, the
plaintiffs filed a suit praying for a decree of permanent injunction
restraining the agents, relatives, defendants from interfering or
encroaching in any manner whatsoever from interfering over the
remaining portion of the property lying in Khasra No. 49, as the sale
deed having executed in their favour by the predecessors of the
plaintiffs/respondents on 29th January, 1966, was limited to 0.77
hectares of land.

5
10. In order to substantiate the case, the
plaintiffs/respondents had described the details of the property in the
plaint map, which constituted the part of the suit, as under :-

6
11. In response to the plaint allegation, the
defendants/appellants had filed the written statement, paper no. 24-A
and, thereafter, the defendant Nos. 2 to 5 had also filed written
statement, paper No. 37-A. They have also simultaneously raised a
claim by filing counter claim under Order 8 Rule 6-A of the C.P.C.
At this stage, it would be relevant to mention that the pleadings raised
by the two different written statements submitted by the defendant
No. 1 and defendant No. 2 to 5, in fact, both the written statements
contained a common pleading in relation to their respective rights,
which they alleged that it has been created by virtue of the sale deed
dated 29th January, 1966, which was absolutely distinct pleadings.
Apart from it, the defendants/appellants had tried to deny the plaint
allegations on the ground that though they admit the fact that the
predecessors of the defendants had purchased only a limited part of
one bigha of land, constituting of 0.77 hectares of khasra No. 49, but
they denied the plaint map by showing that the property thus
conveyed to them as described by figure 'ABCDE' in the map
annexed with the plaint was not correct. Part of the land of the
defendants/appellants, which the defendants/appellants had contended
that it was in fact a patti of land, lying on the Western side adjoining
the road called as 'Gular Ghati Road' and some portion of the
property described by the figure 'ABCDE', according to the
defendants/appellants, the plaintiffs//respondents had sold the patti,
adjoining the road, showing it as to be the part of their property but
they contended that, in fact, the said land was of the Gaon Sabha has
been sold by the plaintiffs/respondents to the predecessors of the
defendants/ appellants, which constituted to be the part of the sale
deed dated 29th January, 1966.
12. They further denied that the plaint averments pertaining
to the survey map, i.e. Tehsildar's report and fixation of the pillars /
khutis on the portion of the property, which according to their
pleading was contended is absolutely a myth which has been
developed by the plaintiffs/respondents for the purposes of suit, in

7
question, and they contended that the plaintiffs/respondents had rather
constructed the wall and had encroached upon the land of the
defendants/appellants when the defendants/appellants were not
present on the spot in question. The defendants/appellants contended
in their written statement that the defendants still continued to hold
their possession over the property, which was sold in their favour by
the predecessors of the plaintiffs/respondents and they contended that
the portion of the property demarcated by figure 'A' and 'B', there
exists a mango tree which has been deliberately not shown in the
plaint map which had demarcated the property which was purchased
by the predecessors of the defendant/appellants. Over the remaining
land, it was the defendants/appellants case that they are operating their
Aata Chaki and in the open space, which was left out of the part of the
property purchased by them, they are using it as a place for dumping
cow dungs.
13. The case of the defendants/appellants was that though
they admit the existence of 3 feet high wall from figure 'A' and 'B',
which was also admitted by the Advocate of the defendants/appellants
to be existing on the spot demarcating the property in dispute, but, in
addition to it, the defendants/appellants case was that the existence of
mango trees, or the wall from figure 'A' and 'B' has not been shown
or detailed in the plaint map. They further denied the allegations
pertaining to the attempt being made by the defendants/appellants for
damaging the wall.
14. In order to file a counter claim seeking an order of
restrained from interference from the plaintiffs/respondents, the
defendants/appellants have come up with the case that as on the
Western side of the property, which adjoins the Gular Ghati Road,
there exists about 20 feet wide patti of land, which belongs to the
Gaon Sabha and that has been wrongly included in their sale deed by
the plaintiffs//respondents by showing it as to be the property which is
vested with them and thus, the defendants/appelants claim in the

8
counter claim was that after deducting the said 20 feet of land
belonging to the Gaon Sabha, if the boundaries of the plaintiffs
property is measured, which admittedly, lies in Gaon Sabha Harawala,
according to the defendants, it would be a lesser property in areas than
which has been sold by the plaintiffs/respondents by wrongly
including in it 20 feet wide patti. The defendants/appellants case was
that Gaon Sabha has already initiated the proceedings and has asked
the District Magistrate to get the land lying in patti may be vacated as
it could not have been conveyed by plaintiffs/respondents since being
the property belonging to the Gaon Sabha and it could not have
constituted as to be the part of the sale deed dated 29th January, 1966.
15. The argument of the learned counsel for the defendants/
appellants pertaining to the extent of sale made by the predecessors of
the plaintiffs being lesser than what has been depicted from the sale
deed on the pretext that according to the allegations leveled by the
defendants, the predecessors of the plaintiffs/ respondents since have
no title over 20 feet wide pati, which existed adjoining to Gular Ghati
Road, no sale deed could have been executed with regard to the said
portion of the property. Hence, they contended that the sale made as
back as on 29th January, 1966, contained a part of the property which
could not have been transferred by the plaintiffs/respondents.
16. In order to attack propriety to the sale deed and the part
which was conveyed by the predecessor of the plaintiffs//respondents,
as per the Explanation 1 to Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act,
it was the responsibility which was to be shouldered by the purchasers
of the land, i.e. the defendants/appellants that prior to entering into the
sale, they ought to have verified the alleged theory which they have
argued now that the plaintiffs /respondents have sold a certain portion
of the Gaon Sabha land (Pati) and thus, if any action was required to
be taken as per the Explanation 1 to judge the propriety of the sale,
and its subject matter, it was to be discharged by the purchaser

9
himself, that he was purchasing the correct property. Explanation 1 to
Section 3 is quoted hereunder :-
"["a person is said to have notice" of a fact when he
actually knows that fact, or when but for wilful abstention from
an enquiry or search which he ought to have made, or gross
negligence, he would have known it.]
Explanation I.-Where any transaction relating to
immovable property is required by law to be and has been
effected by a registered instrument, any person acquiring such
property or any part of, or share or interest in, such property
shall be deemed to have notice of such instrument as from the
date of registration or, where the property is not all situated in
one sub-district, or where the registered instrument has been
registered under sub-section (2) of section 30 of the Indian
Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908), from the earliest date on
which any memorandum of such registered instrument has been
filed by any Sub-Registrar within whose sub-district any part of
the property which is being acquired, or of the property
wherein a share or interest is being acquired, is situated:]
Provided that-
(1) the instrument has been registered and its
registration has been completed in the manner prescribed by
the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908), and the rules
made thereunder,
(2) the instrument or memorandum has been duly entered
or filed, as the case may be, in books kept under section 51 of
that Act, and
(3) the particulars regarding the transaction to which the
instrument relates have been correctly entered in the indexes
kept under section 55 of that Act.
Explanation II.-Any person acquiring any immovable
property or any share or interest in any such property shall be
deemed to have notice of the title, if any, of any person who is
for the time being in actual possession thereof.

10
Explanation III.-A person shall be deemed to have had
notice of any fact if his agent acquires notice thereof whilst
acting on his behalf in the course of business to which that fact
is material: Provided that, if the agent fraudulently conceals
the fact, the principal shall not be charged with notice thereof
as against any person who was a party to or otherwise
cognizant of the fraud."
17. It was also the case of the defendants/appellants that the
sale deed which was executed on 29th January, 1966, by the
predecessors was not sustainable for the reasons that even the Pradhan
of the Gaon Sabha, Mr. Satyapal Singh had also initiated the
proceedings against the defendants/appellants for getting them
vacated from the property occupied by them alleging thereof that it
was the encroachment made by the defendants/appellants over the
Gaon Sabha property, whereas, on the contrary the case of the
defendants/appellants was that they are not the encroachers but rather
they are the actual purchasers from the plaintiffs/respondents and
their possession is confined to the extent of the property which was
sold to them by the plaintiffs/ respondents as back as in 1966.
18. In response to the written statement, the
plaintiffs/respondents had filed their replication, denying the
allegations raised in their written statement as well as in the counter
claim by filing replication which was numbered as Paper No. 27-A.
After the exchange of the pleadings between the parties, the learned
Trial Court had framed the following issues :

19. In support of the contention, the plaintiffs/
respondents had led oral evidence of PW1 Dilip, PW2 Dharam
Singh and PW3 Hubilal, (Exhibit, paper No.10-C), which was
placed before the Court. Besides the oral evidence, the
plaintiffs/respondents has also adduced documentary evidences of
Khatuni, Paper No. 11-C which was exhibit 2, Khasra paper
No. 13 C which was exhibit 5 and the report as submitted to the
Superintendent of Police, as paper No. 14-C and its receipts to
show that the defendants/appellants had made an effort to
encroach upon the property of the plaintiffs/respondents lying in
Northern side, demarcated by the three feet high wall from figure
'A' to 'B'. Apart from the above evidence, the
plaintiffs/respondents have also produced paper No. 17-C, which
was the publication made by the defendants/appellants themselves
in the newspaper on 2nd April, 1997, showing the existence of the
wall from figure 'A' to 'B'.
20. While, on the other hand, to substantiate their case,
the defendants/appellants had produced paper No. 44, i.e. sale deed
as exhibit Ka and paper No. 45 Ga, which was the khatuni of the
land, in dispute, as exhibit Ka 2 and had recorded the oral
testimony of DW1 Ashok Kumar, DW2 Satyapal Singh and DW3
Ratan Mani.

12
21. The learned Trial Court had consolidated the issues
and by the judgment dated 26th July, 2001, had dismissed the Suit
and had decreed the counter claim, thereby restraining the
plaintiffs/ respondents from interfering in any manner over the
property in dispute.
22. On looking to the findings which has been recorded
by the learned Trial Court, which virtually affected the proceedings
of the suit, it was in relation to the findings which was recorded on
issue Nos. 1 and 7 as to who happens to be the actual owner of the
property and also to the effect that whether the property in the suit
was identifiable, if it is read in harmony with the counter claim
raised by the defendants/ appellants, it would be depicting the
actual position which existed.
23. The learned Trial Court had decided the issue Nos.1
and 7 pertaining to the title and most importantly the execution of
the sale deed dated 29th January, 1966, and the sale made of Khasra
No. 49 to the extent of 0.77 hectares to the predecessors of the
defendants/appellants was not disputed. While dealing with the
issue No. 1 and 7, the Trial Court had also recorded a finding that
as per the map submitted by the defendants/respondents in the
written statement, he has shown that the property described by
figure 'ABCDE' was a part of the sale deed of the land which was
executed in his favour and it was also concluded that for the
remaining part of property described by figure 'ABFG', which
extended upto the canal pati in the North belonged to the
plaintiffs/respondents.
24. Another important aspect which can also be visualized
from the findings which has been recorded by the Trial Court was
to the effect that the defendants/appellants had admitted that they
have purchased 0.077 hectares of land from the predecessors of the

13
plaintiffs/ respondents. But they have denied the contention of the
plaintiffs/respondents to the effect that the defendant No.1 had not
sold the property described by figure 'ABFG'. The learned Trial
Court while recording its findings on issue Nos. 1 and 7 has not
considered the oral testimony and the documents, which was
placed on record adduced by the plaintiffs/ respondents and while
appreciating the oral testimony of the defendants/appellants to the
effect that apart from the land, in question, no other property was
sold by the plaintiffs.
25. While considering the statement of DW1 Dilip, DW2
Dharam Singh and DW3 Hubilal, the Trial Court has only
considered the oral testimony of the defendants/appellants
witnesses and has held that the description of the property and its
boundaries as given therein, in fact, in the North-West, there is
Gular Ghati Road. The Trial Court has held that the manner, in
which, the description of the property has been given in the plaint,
it included in it the patti which was claimed by the Gaon Sabha to
be belonging to them which have wrongfully been sold by the
plaintiffs//respondents. On issue No. 2 pertaining to the valuation
of the suit was already decided by the Trial Court on 6th January,
1999, and nobody had challenged the decision rendered on the said
issue.
26. The sole controversy, in question, which is now
confined to it would be depending upon the findings which has
been recorded by the Trial Court in its judgment dated 26th July,
2001, it would be based on the finding, which was recorded on
issue Nos. 6 and 7, pertaining to the description of the property as
given in the plaint map and in the map which has been annexed
with the counter claim.
27. Both the parties to the proceedings, in fact, had denied
the description of the property given in the plaint map by each

14
other and, more particularly, the defendants/appellants had
contended that the Chauhaddi given in the map showing the
existence of the road on the North-western side is wrong. The
learned Trial Court, for the purposes of determining the extent of
the property which was conveyed by the sale deed, had considered
paper No. 44 C, i.e. the sale deed of 29th January, 1966, in which,
in the East, it was shown as a canal; in the West, house of the
plaintiffs and in the North, it is shown, there exists a road.
28. During the course of the proceedings, the Advocate
commission was held by invoking Order 26 Rule 9 of the C.P.C.
and the Advocate Commissioner has submitted his report, paper
No. 29-C, and according to the finding, which has been recorded
by the Trial Court is that the map annexed with the Advocate
Commissioner report, he has also depicted the true extent of the
property which was actually conveyed to the
defendants/appellants. The Trial Court while appreciating the
statement and the oral testimony adduced by the plaintiff witness
as PW3 Hubilal, in which, in its para 2, he has admitted the
situation with regard to the canal which was claimed by the parties
to be flowing from the Southern part of the land which adjoins the
land of Ram Singh. The Court recorded the finding that the
description of the property as given in the report submitted by the
Advocate Commissioner, if compared with the statement of PW3
Hubilal, the Trial Court has recorded the findings, it supports the
contention of the defendants/appellants so far it relates to the
description of the property on the spot and thus, held that the
Commissioner's report, 29-C/5, also stands fortified by the map of
the defendants/appellants and it also stands fortified if compared
with the statements of defendants witnesses.
29. The learned Trial Court while deciding issue Nos. 6
and 8 had taken into consideration that when despite of the
demarcation report and the report of Advocate Commissioner, 29-

15
C/5, when the dispute pertaining to the exact location of the land is
still continuing to be the bone of contention between the parties,
late Mr. Haveli Ram is said to have issued the notices on 2nd April,
1997. In the examination in chief, Dilip Kumar, i.e. PW1, on an
appraisal of his oral testimony has recorded the finding that it
supports of the contention that the wall was as shown from point A
to B was existing since 1977, and it was constructed only in 1997,
and hence, the Trial Court held that the statement made that the
wall was about 20 years old, stands denied. The learned Trial
Court while deciding issue No. 1 pertaining to Section 34 of the
Specific Relief Act held that the suit, in question, would be barred
by Section 34. Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act reads as
under:-
"34. Discretion of court as to declaration of status or
right.-Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any
right as to any property, may institute a suit against any
person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such
character or right, and the court may in its discretion make
therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff
need not in such suit ask for any further relief: Provided that
no court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff,
being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of
title, omits to do so.
Explanation.-A trustee of property is a "person
interested to deny" a title adverse to the title of some one
who is not in existence, and whom, if in existence, he would
be a trustee."
30. The plaintiffs have stated that since the
defendants/appellants in his counter claim had not sought
possession of the property in dispute, hence, their claim would be
barred by Section 34 of the Act. However, the finding pertaining
to the possession of the property conveyed to the
defendants/appellants by the plaintiffs/respondents, and its extent

16
was recorded in their favour and also the finding in relation to the
existence of their Aata Chaki, and the existence of the trees on the
spot, in question, which Trial Court has held that as per the map
annexed with the sale deed, the bar as pleaded emanating from
Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, would not come into play.
Ultimately, the learned Trial Court while deciding issue Nos. 4 and
13 has held that since the plaintiffs/ respondents has admitted that
late Shahbudin had sold the property which is the fact which is not
denied by the PWs' adduced before the Court below, and since
they have not denied that the defendants/appellants are in
possession of 1 bigha of land purchased by the predecessors of the
defendants, the Trial Court has recorded that the
plaintiffs/respondents have got no concern in relation to the
property which was sold by the predecessors to the
defendants/appellants, as it stood established by the evidence
adduced by the defendants/appellants to which no contrary
evidence was produced by the plaintiffs/respondents to show that
the sale deed was not executed in relation to the property, in
question , i.e. khasra no. 49, having an area of 0.77 hectares which
was sold to the predecessors of the defendants/appellants.
Consequently, the Suit was dismissed and the counter claim was
decreed and the plaintiffs/respondents were restrained by way of
decree of permanent injunction from interference in the piece of
land of the defendant/respondent No. 1 in any manner whatsoever,
whereas, the counter claim filed by defendants No. 2 to 5 was
rejected. The resultant effect of its rejection would be that as far
as defendant Nos. 2 to 5 are concerned, their claim of possession
over the property which constituted to be the part of the land sold
by sale deed which was conveyed by the predecessors of the
plaintiffs was rejected and their claim over the property has
attained finality because the defendant Nos. 2 to 5 after the
rejection of the counter claim, which has to be treated as to be a
specific plaint has not been put to challenge by filing an
independent appeal.

17
31. Being aggrieved against the judgment dated 26th July,
2001, the plaintiffs/respondents had preferred a Civil Appeal under
Section 96 of the C.P.C. In the memorandum of the First Appeal
as preferred by the plaintiffs/respondents against the dismissal of
the suit and decreeing of the counter claim of defendant No. 1,
after considering the rival contentions, had decreed the suit of the
plaintiffs/respondents and dismissed the counter claim of the
defendant No.1, deceased Haveli Ram.
32. In the Appeal, in question, the plaintiffs/respondents
had contended that the judgment of the Trial Court dated 26th July,
2001, is vitiated from the view point that :
(i) Admittedly, the sale made by the predecessors
of the plaintiffs//respondents, which was only
limited to the extent of one bigha of land,
whereas, as per the reports of the Commissioner
and the revenue authorities, placed on record,
the defendants/ respondents have been shown to
be in possession of in excess of land, which was
equivalent to 1 bigha 6 biswas, which is
absolutely not in consonance to the sale deed
with regard to the extent of property conveyed
to them, which was only one bigha, i.e.0.77
hectares of land.
(ii) Even the case as projected before the Trial
Court by the defendants/appellants, when they
themselves admit vesting of the title over one
bigha of land only and which they have
supported it from the map annexed with the
written statement and which also stands
established by the map annexed with Advocate
Commissioner's report which was made part of

18
the record, but still, the learned Trial Court
without rightfully appreciating the evidence on
record, had come to the conclusion to the effect
that the sale was made way back in 1966, since
the sale itself was not questioned ever which
showed existence of the Gular Ghati Road on
the North-western side of the property thus
conveyed by the figure 'ABCDE'. At a later
stage, they cannot contend that the sale which
has been made by the predecessor of the
plaintiffs wrongfully included a 20 feet wide
patti of the alleged land, said to be belonging to
the Gaon Sabha of Miawala and thus it is the
mistake which has been committed by the Trial
Court which runs contrary to the records.
(iii) It was the case of the appellants that no khasra
number or khatuni or any other evidence was
placed on record by the defendants/appellants
before the First Appellate Court to show that 20
feet wide patti was belonging to the Gaon
Sabha Miawala.
(iv) It was the case of the appellants that out of the
total land of khasra number 49, which was
having an area of 0.194 hectares, only a piece
of land out of it, i.e. one bigha, i.e. equivalent to
0.77 hectares was sold and it was exclusively
only on that piece of land, over which, the
defendant/appellants could have raised the
claim.
(v) Because even as per the map, which was
constituting to be the part of the sale deed as
well as the map which was annexed with the
plaint, it showed the extent of the property
which constituted to be the part of the sale

19
deed, which excluded the portion of the
property which fell with Gular Ghati Road
which was shown to be existing on the North
western part of the property sold to the
defendants/appellants. The Court held that the
defendants/appellants cannot take advantage of
an excess of the land beyond the sale deed, and
had filed a false map in support of their written
statement.
33. The learned Trial Court also considered the statement
of DW1, as well as the map on which he has placed reliance along
with the written statement, in which, on the northern side, the
defendants/appellants have shown the existence of the Gular Ghati
Road as would be apparent from the map annexed with the counter
claim.
34. Thus the Appellate Court has held that as per the
admitted facts submitted on record, based on the appreciation of
the Advocate Commissioner's report and map submitted by the
plaintiffs/respondents, the plea taken by the defendants/appellants,
that the sale deed so made by the predecessors of the
plaintiffs/respondents was by including the land belonging to the
Gaon Sabha Miawala, it is not proved by the
defendants/appellants by any independent evidence because
according to their map of sale deed of 1966, itself had shown the
existence of Gular Ghati Road on the north western side.
35. The Appellate Court has held that even if the
contention of the appellants is taken into consideration, then too, as
per the sale deed and map annexed with it on both the sides of the
property, thus sold, which constituted to be part of sale deed of
1966, the road was required to be shown, but in fact, from the
maps, which was placed on record, the road was shown only

20
existing on the north western side and thus the Appellate Court
held that the contentions of the defendant No. 1/appellant that the
land upto extent of the road on the eastern side would also fall into
his share of property is untenable because if that part of the
property is included, it would increase the total area of land for
which sale was made by the plaintiffs/ respondents.
36. The Appellate Court, while considering the evidence
has held that so called road existing on the both side of the
property sold to the defendant/appellants was existing about for
more than 100 years back and hence, the Trial Court has wrongly
appreciated the evidence by contending that after the Gular Ghati
Road, there existed 20 feet wide patti of Gaon Sabha Miawala,
which was not proved by the defendant/appellants on record to
show that it was a land constituting to be the part of the sale deed
dated 29th January, 1966, executed by the predecessors of the
plaintiff/respondents in their favour. Hence, the plea of the
defendants/appellants to the effect that the predecessors of the
plaintiff respondents had wrongfully sold 20 feet wide patti of
Gaon Sabha Miawala to defendant/appellants was not established
by the evidence nor it was ever the case of the Gaon Sabha of
Miawala regarding any claim of existence of 20 feet wide patti
adjoining the Gular Ghati Road and, more particularly, when as per
the map of sale deed of 1966, in the sale deed itself it shows that in
the north western side, it was Gular Ghati Road and thereafter, the
property which was conveyed to the defendants/appellants by the
sale deed of 1966, was adjoining to the road itself. Meaning there
was no intervening land between the road and land purchased by
defendants/appellants.
37. The Appellate Court has recorded the finding that in
the proceedings of measurement as held by the Assistant Record
officer at the two stages, before the Trial Court, which was
conducted in the presence of the defendant appellants also, the

21
width of Gular Ghati Road has been shown to be of 30-32 feet
wide belonging to the P.W.D. and the pillar which has been
installed by the revenue authorities, at point exactly adjoins the
road and hence, the Trial Court has wrongly appreciated the oral
testimony of the witnesses of the plaintiffs, wherein, they have
placed reliance on the Advocate Commissioner Report and the
report of the assistant record officer, with regard to the existence of
the road and the land of the defendants.
38. Even the Appellate Court has also scrutinized the map
submitted by the Advocate Commissioner, being paper No. 29-
A/5, and considered the map which showed the existence of the
property by figure 'AEJH'. In fact, even in the map annexed by
the Advocate Commissioner, it did not show anywhere the
existence of the so called 20 feet wide patti which the
defendants/appellants claimed to be existing belonging to the Gaon
Sabha Miawala and thus, the Appellate Court held that the very
finding recorded by the Trial Court pertaining to the extent of the
land sold to the defendants/ appellants, it included 20 feet wide
patti, which was land of Gaon Sabha of Maiwala, was contrary to
the evidence on record and even contrary to the claim raised by the
Gaon Sabha of Miawala, itself.
39. The Appellate Court has further recorded findings that
the Trial Court has arrived to a conclusion that there existed 20 feet
wide patti adjoining Miawala road and, thereafter, the property
which constituted to be the part of sale deed of 1966, it is also
based on only a statement of the Gram Pradhan of Miawala and it
is on his saying that said fact was believed by the Trial Court and
has recorded a finding that 20 feet wide patti could not have been
sold by the predecessors of the plaintiffs/ respondents.
40. The Appellate Court had held that since in the absence
of there being any evidence, which was relied by the Advocate

22
Commissioner in his report, apart from the statement of Gram
Pradhan, it cannot be believed that the un-assailed sale made as
back as in 1966, included 20 wide patti adjoining Gular Ghati
Road thereby reducing the area of land sold to the defendants/
appellants.
41. The Appellate Court further while considering the
statement of DW2 Satyapal Singh has submitted that the inference
which has been drawn by the Trial Court is contrary to the
statement of DW2 for the reason, that apart from the fact that it
was not supported by any evidence and that the burden to prove to
show that Khasra Nos. 282 and 283 belonged to the Gaon Sabha
Miawala which adjoins the Gular Ghati Road was a burden which
was to be discharged by the defendants/appellants, which they
failed to do so in view of the provisions contained under Section
103 of the Evidence Act, hence, their contention was not accepted.
42. Ultimately, the Appellate Court held that the Trial
Court had erred in law by wrongfully appreciating the oral
testimony of defendant No. 2 and the findings recorded on issue
Nos. 1 and 7 is perverse and is contrary to the evidence on record
and the plaint map as well as the report of the revenue authorities
which was held twice, which showed the exact existence of the
property, and which as per the defendants/appellants evidence
also, which the defendants/appellants tried to disclose by virtue of
the map annexed with the counter claim, they have not disclosed
the exact measurement of the property and its periphery and taking
the said map as not to be giving a correct location of the property
and accepting that map, the learned Trial Court has misread the
evidence on record and a wrongful conclusion has been drawn by
the Trial Court while deciding issue Nos. 6 and 8.
43. The Appellant Court, ultimately, on considering the
rival contentions of the parties have come to the conclusion that as

23
per the evidence on record, Khasra No. 49, constitutes to be having
an area of 0.194 hectares, which on the Northern side adjoins the
canal patti, shown by figure 'F' and 'G' and the
defendant/appellant No. 1 since his rights were confined only in
relation to the property purchased by him to the extent of 0.77
hectares in 1966, on which, there existed his House, Aata Chaki,
Dhan Machine and open space for dumping cow dungs, etc. has
been rightly described in the plaint map by figure 'ABCDE'.
44. The Appellate Court further recorded a finding that
after the death of Shahbuddin on 4th November, 1996, the
substituted heirs of the plaintiffs/ respondents have been duly
recorded in the revenue records over the remaining part of the
property shown by the figure 'ABEFG', which was being sought to
be interfered by the defendants/appellants by forcefully occupying
the same.
45. The Appellate Court had further assigned a logic
while reversing the judgment of the Trial Court dated 26th July,
2001, holding thereof that the contention of the
defendants/appellants cannot be accepted because at the time when
the plaintiffs/ respondents were raising construction of the wall
from figure 'A' to 'B' as shown in the plaint map to demarcate the
property sold and the property left over with the plaintiffs/
respondents, none of the defendants/appellants had ever raised any
objections at the relevant point of time, when the wall from point
A to B was being constructed. Another important aspect which
has been taken into consideration by the Appellate Court is that
even as per the notice which was sent by the defendants/appellants
on 4th November, 1996, in the said notice too, the defendants had
shown the existence of the wall on figure 'A' to 'B'. The
Appellate Court has also considered and recorded the finding that
on a comparative scrutiny of the plaint map, the map annexed with
the counter claim, the map submitted by the Advocate

24
Commissioner, there does not happen to be a massive distinction
pertaining to the extent of rights created in favour of the
defendants/appellants by the sale deed of 1966 and none of the
maps has been denied by the parties showing the existence of the
demarcation wall shown from figure 'A' to 'B' and even the
consecutive measurement done by the revenue authorities at the
stage of trial reiterated the status of the property in both the
reports, which was found to be as per the map of the sale deed
itself, which have been submitted by the revenue officials. Even
the Appellate Court has recorded the finding that the philosophy of
inclusion of the land of Gaon Sabha, Miawala into the land which
was said to have been conveyed to the defendants/appellants by the
plaintiffs/ respondents, is not depicting the correct measurement of
the property because even when the survey was conducted by the
Survey Map Naib Tehsildar, no distinction in the measurement was
shown or reported by him for wall shown from figure 'A' and 'B',
which, in fact, demarcated the property. The finding of the
Appellant Court to the effect that the existence of 3 feet height wall
and the existence of the passage to the property of the
plaintiffs//respondents and the defendants/appellants and also the
opening on Gular Ghati Road, is a fact which is not disputed by
any of the parties to the proceedings, because after crossing the
road, lies khasra Nos. 382 and 383 on the Southern side which
belongs to the Gram Sabha Harawala. The Appellate Court while
appreciating the exhibit-1, which was produced by the
defendants/appellants, it is by their own evidence which goest to
show that the property which was purchased by the predecessor of
the defendants/appellants on the Eastern side, adjoining to the
property conveyed shows the canal on the East, on the West there
is a house and in the North, there is a road and then a canal and on
the Southern side, it shows the property of the defendant/
appellants. Even while appreciating the map of the
defendants/respondents filed along with the counter claim and the
boundary which has been shown therein, if compared with the

25
Advocate Commissioner's report and map, paper No. 29-Ga, it
fortifies the actual area of the property sold in 1966 to the
defendants/appellants. The Appellate Court, while appreciating
the findings recorded on issue Nos. 6 and 8, the map submitted by
both the parties in support of their pleadings, shows concurrence
with the map of the Advocate Commissioner. Apart from it, the
statement of PW3 Hubilal, it too shows the existence of a canal on
the Eastern side which shows that the argument extended by the
defendants/appellants in relation to the property described by him
in the map annexed with the counter claim, has rightly described
the property which was actually conveyed by the predecessors of
the plaintiffs//respondents and there existed no patti of 20 feet wide
land belonging to Gaon Sabha Miawala.
46. During the pendency of the Appeal, the
appellants/defendants had filed an application under Order 41
Rule 27 of the C.P.C., wherein, they have placed on record certain
documents pertaining to the khatuni of 1400 fasli of Khata No.
419, which recorded the plaintiff/respondent Raj Kumar and
others. They have also placed on record, paper No. 40-Ga, i.e.
certified copy of the khatuni of 1400 fasli of khata No.705 of
Haveliram and also the punirikshit khasra, paper No. 42-C and 42-
C/2 and khasara Muntikeb as well as paper No. 43-Ga, i.e. the
certified copy of the fard muntikev, pertaining to sajra of 1345
fasli, which showed that in accordance with the survey of khasara
No. 49, it showed that the old khasra No. 49 which was sold in
1966, several small khasra numbers have been carved out by now,
for example, khasra no. 16, khasra No. 71, on which, there exists
the houses of other tenure holders. On scrutiny of the document,
the Appellate Court concluded that on perusal of the punirikshit
khatuni 39-ka and 40 kha, it establishes that the predecessors of the
defendants/appellants Haveli Ram, the parts sold to him has been
recorded in punirikshit khatuni as Khasra No. 16, shown in khatuni
of plot No. 705 and remaining part has been shown in khasra 14-

26
kha, 15 and 17. Hence, the Court held that on punirikshit survey
and due to a separate khasra numbers being assigned to the
principal khasra no. 49, out of which khasra No. 16, which has
been allotted to the defendants/appellants, which was done in
pursuance to the order of the State Government and after hearing
all the parties concerned and, hence after the preparation of the
punirikshit survey, the defendants/appellants is shown to be in
possession over the extent of the property which was purchased by
them in 1966, and consequently, after considering the impact of the
punirikshit khautni, which was a consequence of the punirikshit
survey, an allocation of khasra No. 16 of the land purchased by the
defendants/appellants and reading it in co-relation to the maps
submitted by the parties to the suit as compared with that of the
Advocate Commissioner report which was not objected by the
defendants/appellants, it was held by the Appellate Court that the
defendants/ appellants happen to be in possession of 0.077 hectares
of land which was purchased by the predecessors of the
defendants/appellants and, hence, they were not entitled for any
decree of injunction of possession as claimed in the counter claim
and the Appellate Court has rightly allowed the appeal, whereby,
based on the punirikshit survey, it was held that the parties are in
possession of respective parts of the land which they were entitled
to hold legally and thus, it was ultimately concluded that none of
the parties would interfere over the part and parcel of the land
which has been settled down in the punirikshit survey and,
consequently, the suit for injunction was partially decreed by the
impugned judgment dated 7th May, 2019.
47. In view of the findings which has been recorded by
the Appellate Court which is based upon a sound appreciation of
evidence and also the effect of the subsequent survey, which was
conducted by the Revenue Authorities and considering the entries
made by the competent revenue authorities in punirikshit khasras,
the Appellate Court has rightly decreed the Suit because as per the

27
finding recorded on appreciation of evidence, all the parties have
been found to be in possession of their respective part and parcel of
the land. Thus, this Court is of the view that the Second Appeal is
concluded by the findings of fact and it does not entail
consideration of any substantial question of law. Hence, the
Second Appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
48. However, there would be no order as to costs.
